observations.text: Gangway watch not in place when he boarded: cadet on the gangway, duty AB and pumpman elsewhere. Discussed for 10 minutes before the opening meeting.
Hose handling crane hydraulic hose spares: PMS listed one complete set; each hose should be listed with part number and kept secured (locked box) against accidental use.

positives: Bosun and fitter answered correctly (positive remark)
style: Judges the ship from the first minute at the gangway
Checks every page of the bunker checklist
Tests things live: each overfill warning light, emergency generator spring start then battery start, random lamp tests
Interviews ratings in depth in the CCR, then checks their answers with officers
Will issue STOP for unsafe acts during rounds (pumpman walking over mooring lines)

questions.q: How do you report when equipment related to class fails?
What does the marking on the brake handle spindle mean? What happens before or beyond the mark?
Where is the Bosun's mooring station, how many people are there and who is involved? Are oilers included? Where is the mooring plan?
Where is your mooring station, how many people with you, who operates the winch?
What is your duty in enclosed space entry? What do you check, who else checks, who signs the permit, what equipment do you bring?
How do you check the atmosphere? (stop the fan, wait 5 to 10 minutes)
You signed the mooring plan training record. Did you read the plan?
After loading, shore asks for a sample or ullage of a cargo tank. What do you do and why?
Why wait 30 minutes after loading before sampling or ullaging?
How is the enclosed space risk assessment and permit filled in?
How often are ballast tanks and cargo tanks inspected?
When was the last tank cleaning, how was it done, which tank kept the wash water?
How many gas instruments are on board? Show one and calibrate it.
Show the hose crane hydraulic hose spares and compare with the PMS.
What is the hot work procedure in the designated area? How far from an oil tank? Who completes the checklist? What is needed for hot work outside the workshop? What do you check before starting?
Show the UMS checklist, arrival and departure checklists, C/E standing orders and port order book.
Show the insulation mat certificate. What are the 220 V and 440 V low insulation readings?

checks.item: Last PSC, USCG and SIRE reports
CMS progress shown by C/O and 2/E
Last mooring line break test report, how it was done, where the equipment is
Every page of the bunker checklist
LO analysis reports and Oil Record Book Part I
Cargo tank high level and overfill alarms on two wing tanks, every warning light
Ballast tank vents, deck seal level, PV breaker, oxygen and acetylene rooms, paint store explosion proof light, sample locker, SOPEP locker
Both lifeboats
Bosun store bilge well alarms port and starboard
Emergency generator: spring start first, then battery start
Life jackets and immersion suits: zips operated
Liferafts, EPIRB, SART, compass deck, random repeater and panel lamp tests
Ballast water treatment system operation
Cargo plan stage against actual tank levels
Remote manifold pressure reading compared with the gauge at the manifold
ODME decanting printout and Oil Record Book Part II
Alarms tried: ER bilge wells, ME FO leak off, generator FO leak off, ME oil mist detector, OWS recirculation
Random eye wash stations and EEBDs, ME emergency manoeuvring and Hypermist panel lamp tests
Fire locker, change room, laundry, hospital
Foam tank level gauge free of air bubbles (from previous SIRE)

tips: Have the gangway watch exactly as per the port watch orders from the moment the inspector can arrive
Keep the Bosun able to explain the mooring plan he signed for
Ratings must know why you wait after loading before sampling (static electricity)
List hydraulic hose spares one by one with part numbers and keep them locked
Clear any item from the previous SIRE before this one: he checks them
summary: Started badly at the gangway and he discussed it before the opening meeting. After that a thorough, hands-on inspection: every overfill light, emergency generator starts, live alarm tests and long CCR interviews with the Bosun. Two observations, and a positive remark for the Bosun and fitter.
